video_goal: Demonstrate the visual process of brewing coffee using a Bialetti moka pot and Stumptown Hair Bender beans.
required_subjects_and_props: Bialetti moka pot, Stumptown Hair Bender coffee bag, coffee grounds, hot water kettle, stovetop burner, kitchen towel, ceramic mug, coffee scoop.

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place a bag of Stumptown Hair Bender coffee next to a disassembled aluminum Bialetti moka pot on a wooden countertop.
Hands pour steaming hot water from a gooseneck kettle into the bottom water chamber of the Bialetti, stopping exactly at the brass safety valve.
Fingers drop the funnel-shaped metal filter basket into the water-filled bottom chamber.
A metal scoop transfers medium-fine Stumptown Hair Bender coffee grounds from the bag into the filter basket, mounding it slightly.
An index finger sweeps across the top of the filter basket, leveling the coffee grounds flat without tamping or pressing them down.
Hands grip the bottom chamber with a folded kitchen towel and tightly screw the top octagonal chamber onto the base.
Hands place the assembled Bialetti moka pot onto a gas stovetop burner and turn the knob to ignite a medium flame.
A hand flips the lid of the Bialetti open, revealing the empty upper chamber and the central metal spout.
Thick, dark liquid begins to slowly ooze out of the central spout and pool in the bottom of the upper chamber.
The liquid stream turns golden-blond and begins to bubble and sputter rapidly from the spout.
A hand quickly grabs the black plastic handle, removes the Bialetti from the burner, and flips the lid closed.
Hands wrap a damp cloth around the bottom chamber of the Bialetti, producing a small hiss of steam to halt the brewing process.
Hands tilt the Bialetti moka pot, pouring the freshly brewed coffee into a white ceramic mug.
